validated_results.title: A 24-year prospective study of dietary α-linolenic acid and lethal prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of men with validated dietary α-linolenic acid intake and hazard ratios for incident lethal prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: top vs bottom quintile of ALA intake (pre-PSA era)
extraction.timing: pre-diagnosis dietary assessment with 24-year prospective follow-up (1986-2010)
extraction.population: men aged 40-75 years without prior cancer in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study

sample_size.excerpt: 47,885 men aged 40-75 years without prior cancer in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study were prospectively followed from 1986 to 2010.

cases.excerpt: 386 lethal prostate cancers were diagnosed in the pre-PSA era (before February, 1994) and 403 cancers in the PSA era.

effect_size.excerpt: Intake of ALA was associated with increased risk of lethal prostate cancer in the pre-PSA era (comparing top to bottom quintile of intake, multivariate-adjusted HR = 1.78; 95% CI = 1.22-2.06; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.003), but not in the PSA era (HR = 0.81; 95% CI = 0.56-1.17; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.53), and the difference in associations was statistically significant (p for interaction = 0.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Intake of ALA was associated with increased risk of lethal prostate cancer in the pre-PSA era (comparing top to bottom quintile of intake, multivariate-adjusted HR = 1.78; 95% CI = 1.22-2.06; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.003), but not in the PSA era (HR = 0.81; 95% CI = 0.56-1.17; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.53), and the difference in associations was statistically significant (p for interaction = 0.02).

p_value.excerpt: Intake of ALA was associated with increased risk of lethal prostate cancer in the pre-PSA era (comparing top to bottom quintile of intake, multivariate-adjusted HR = 1.78; 95% CI = 1.22-2.06; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.003), but not in the PSA era (HR = 0.81; 95% CI = 0.56-1.17; p<sub>trend</sub> = 0.53), and the difference in associations was statistically significant (p for interaction = 0.02).
